entry.title: ▶️ The desk
entry.content:
▶️ The desk

🚀 Galaxy Hunt 🐂 The Oregon Trail 🗡️ Hack 🖥️ Witch I 🖥️ Basic I

18 October 2026. The page caught up with the glass.

Every game opens from a button. ▶️ Play fills the screen. Escape brings the site back. Witch I and Basic I say 🖥️ Boot, because they are computers, and the lines stay when you leave.

📜 Manual sits beside that button. Getting Started, and the tutorial on Basic I, sit there too. The banner for the game is under the buttons. The words are under the banner.

Home and About open on the site banner. The releases carry the banners of the games they name.

The glass is the current emoji engine. A desk page hides that engine’s own fullscreen button, because Escape already ends the session.
entry.summary: Play or Boot, a manual beside it, and the banner under the buttons.

entry.title: 🕹️ The glass
entry.content:
🕹️ The glass

🚀 Galaxy Hunt 🐂 The Oregon Trail 🗡️ Hack 🏓 Pong 🐍 Snake 🗡️ Rogue 🌲 Adventureland 🏴‍☠️ Pirate Adventure 🤖 Trump Super Intelligence

17 October 2026. Return to begin. R to go again.

The playable games now draw on the emoji engine. Each one, except the conversation, opens on a title. Return leaves it. If you win, or if you die, the last screen says so, and R starts that game again without the title.

Trump Super Intelligence is not a match. It has no title and no ending. You type, it answers, the face follows the mood.

Featured

The Games menu carries three. The catalog still has the rest, with those three first.

Galaxy Hunt is the starship. Eight by eight, raiders, outposts, and a stardate. Dock to repair. HELP is the manual.

The Oregon Trail keeps the trail it already had. The new screen is only the title in front of it. Return still means Return, once you are on the road.

Hack is the dungeon with rooms and a bestiary. A better weapon gets wielded. Armor soaks a hit. P drinks a potion. The Amulet of Yendor is on the sixth floor, and picking it up is the win.

The others

Pong and Snake are no longer a text box. Paddles, a ball, a snake, apples, and the furniture. Snake clears the board at one hundred.

Rogue is the shorter delve: rooms, corridors, six floors, the amulet at the bottom. Q drinks.

Adventureland wants the thirteen treasures in the stump. The bees, the dragon, the bear, and the hole will end it if you insist.

Pirate Adventure wants the three treasures back in the London flat. The skeleton does not share, unless the parrot has heard the words.
entry.summary: The games move onto the emoji engine. Three of them lead the shelf.

entry.title: 🖥️ Witch I, the add-on
entry.content:
🖥️ Witch I, the add-on

🖥️ Witch I

17 October 2026. The same computer. The box learned a few more tricks.

She shipped on the 16th. This is not another Witch I. The programs left the script and moved into shelf/, and the extension is .wasic. SHELF reads the catalog and opens it on the glass. Up and down move the mark. Enter takes that program down and does not run it. She tells you that a number changes a line. Escape leaves the shelf where it is.

HELLO-WITCH and HELLO-DEMON are the two hellos. CAROL hums. FAMILIAR paces. ANSI-WITCH is a picture. VEIL sends the glass its own color codes: the sixteen, the 256, and a color mixed on the spot. LIST prints the program. The line numbers are yellow. Retype one, and that line is the new line.

When the glass wakes, she draws herself in those colors, hat first. Two low notes, and the drawing steps aside for the portrait and the count. Then the words roll up and the glass says SPEAK.

Under the glass, the keys are an emoji, a word, and a function key. LIST, RUN, SHELF, SCRUB, MAGIC, EXORCISE, LATCH. Nothing there is a button. She wakes latched. Up walks the lines that rolled off the glass. LATCH OFF opens it. F7 and Scroll Lock do what LATCH does.

EXORCISE rewrites a BASIC listing into WASIC. PRINT becomes CHANT, GOTO becomes FLYTO, FOR becomes CURSE, and the rest of the old names follow. INT, SIN, RND, and the other sums stay. PEEK answers 0. A line she still cannot say is buried as a whisper, and RUN steps over it. An empty circle opens the desk for a .BAS file. She leaves the lines sitting there. You run them.

A refusal is red, with a mark, and two notes going down. The walls she keeps are in SYSTEM.md.

Witch I.
entry.summary: The shelf points, she draws herself, and EXORCISE drives BASIC out. One machine, not a second debut.

entry.title: 🖥️ Basic I
entry.content:
🖥️ Basic I

🖥️ Basic I

17 October 2026. A computer for learning.

Basic I is the other 40-column machine. Forty columns, twenty-four rows, and room for 512 lines. The prompt is READY. A line with a number is stored. A line without one runs now.

MODULES opens the lessons that shipped in the box. Getting Started is the first hour. The tutorial walks the rest. The manual is every word this computer knows.

Boot fills the screen. Escape ends the session and brings the page back. Boot again and the lines you stored are still there. A program that was running has stopped.

She is not this machine. Witch I speaks WASIC and keeps 666 lines. Basic I says READY, and the lessons are the point.
entry.summary: The same glass as Witch I. The prompt is READY. The lessons are built in.

entry.title: 🧙 A Witch’s Tale
entry.content:
🧙 A Witch’s Tale

🧙 A Witch's Tale

16 October 2026. A chapter, and a save.

A Witch’s Tale is a tile RPG told in parts. You are a witch. The land has problems. The first chapter is a cottage, a yard, and the trees south of it.

You wake with very little. The wards on the door have gone quiet. A crow at the window has opinions. Something that should not be there took the iron key off the nail and went into the woods. The far gate still wants that key.

Arrows or WASD move. T talks. L looks. Combat is a strike, a spark, or a step back. If you fall, you wake in the bed. The flags you set stay set.

The game stores your chapter, your place, your health, and those flags in this browser. When a chapter ends it looks for the next numbered folder. Chapter 02 is not written yet. The save waits.

That is ten games on the shelf.
entry.summary: Chapter 01 of a tile RPG. A cold kettle, a crow, and a key that walked off.

entry.title: 🖥️ Witch I
entry.content:
🖥️ Witch I

🖥️ Witch I

16 October 2026. She woke up.

Witch I is a small computer on a black glass. Forty columns, twenty-four rows, a line number, and SPEAK.

The language is WASIC. CHANT writes a line. DEMAND asks. CURSE and BREAK count. FLYTO jumps. A line with a number is stored, junk included. A BASIC word fails when she reaches it. PEEK, POKE, and SYS make her complain. She is Witch I. One.

SHELF lists what shipped in the box: HELLO, GUESS, DICE, OMEN, CIRCLES, MINIONS, KEYS. UNSEAL "shelf:GUESS" loads one. RUN starts it. Escape stops it.

SEAL keeps a program in this browser. GRIMOIRE prints the words.

entry.title: 🤖 Trump Super Intelligence
entry.content:
🤖 Trump Super Intelligence

🤖 Trump Super Intelligence

16 October 2026. The rest of the shelf.

Trump Super Intelligence is not a port, and it is not a model. You type a line, press Enter, and it answers from a pile of written replies. The line you typed is matched against a list of words. Praise, insults, China, the news, winning, a greeting: each one has its own stack of answers, and the game picks one.

The face above the text is part of the answer. Five pictures. Happy, smug, ranting, winning, and a neutral that does not get much use, because the default mood is smug. Call it great and the face softens. Call it a liar, a fake, or a fool and it rants, and the little square-wave noise drops in pitch like something powering down in a bad mood.

There is no score and no win. There is a cursor. Many people are saying that is the whole game.

That is the shelf as of today. Pong through Hack are the four days before this one. The catalog has all eight.
entry.summary: A terminal chatbot with five faces, a square wave, and a lot of opinions.

entry.title: 🐂 The Oregon Trail
entry.content:
🐂 The Oregon Trail

🐂 The Oregon Trail

16 October 2026. A wagon, and the long way west.

The Oregon Trail is a terminal homage to the 1985 Apple II game. The screen keeps that shape. “You may:”, a number, RETURN. The words are written for this shelf.

The year is 1848. The road runs from Independence, Missouri, to the Willamette Valley, a little over two thousand miles if you take the long forks. The party is five people. You name all five. The first name is the wagon leader.

Who you are

A banker from Boston starts with $1600. The score at the end stands as scored. A carpenter from Ohio starts with $800, and the score is doubled. A farmer from Illinois starts with $400, and the score is tripled. A score is written only when the wagon reaches the valley.

You can leave in March, April, May, June, or July. March is cold and early. July is a bet against snow in the Blue Mountains.

Matt’s General Store

A yoke is two oxen and costs $40. Matt recommends three. Food is twenty cents a pound, and the wagon holds 2000 pounds. Clothing is $10 a set. Ammunition is $2 a box of 20 bullets. A spare wheel, axle, or tongue is $10.

Forts sell the same goods, and the price rises as you go west. Fort Kearney is a quarter over Matt. Fort Laramie is half again. Fort Bridger is three quarters over. Fort Hall is double. Fort Boise is two and a quarter times the Independence price. Fort Walla Walla is two and a half.

On the trail

The daily menu is the same nine choices.

  1. Continue. The wagon rolls a day at a time. RETURN sizes up the situation and stops.
  2. Check supplies.
  3. Look at the map.
  4. Change pace. Steady is half of what the oxen can do, strenuous is three quarters, grueling is all of it. Four healthy oxen, steady, on the plains, cover about twenty miles. Past Fort Laramie a hard day tops out near twenty-four.
  5. Change rations. Filling is three pounds a person a day, meager is two, bare bones is one.
  6. Rest, up to twenty days.
  7. Trade.
  8. Hunt. Arrows or WASD move. Space shoots, and each shot is one bullet. Q goes back to the wagon. You can carry 100 pounds back.
  9. Matt’s, while you are still in Independence. Buy supplies, at a fort. Talk to people, everywhere else.

Q on that menu asks if you want to abandon the trail. Ctrl-S toggles the sound.

Rivers give the old choices: ford, caulk the wagon and float it, wait, or ask how deep it is. The Kansas has a ferry for $5. The Big Blue has no ferry. The Snake stays deep, and a guide there wants three sets of clothing, or $25. A crossing that goes badly still puts you on the far bank. It can take food, clothing, a spare part, an ox, cash, or a person.

Where the road splits

South Pass. Fort Bridger is the longer road and has a store. The Green River cutoff is shorter, and the crossing is the price of those miles.

The Blue Mountains. Fort Walla Walla can still sell you supplies. The cutoff to The Dalles has no store.

The Dalles. The Barlow Road is a $5 toll and a hundred mountain miles. The Columbia is a raft. Arrows steer. The channel opens on the right. Miss it and you still reach Oregon, with less food.

The end of the road

Health runs from good down through fair, poor, and very poor. Rest and full meals pull a party back. The trail can hand you cholera, dysentery, typhoid, measles, fever, exhaustion, a broken bone, or a snake. If the wagon leader dies, the screen says so in the old way: YOU HAVE DIED OF, and then the cause. The rest of the party can press on. When the whole party is dead, the run ends with no score.

A score counts the living, their health, the wagon, the oxen, the spare parts, the clothing, the bullets, the food, and the cash left, then multiplies by the profession. The Oregon Top Ten stays in this browser. The list starts with names from the emigration. R starts another run.

That is nine games on the shelf.
entry.summary: A terminal homage to the 1985 Apple II trail, from Independence to the Willamette.

entry.title: 🗡️ Rogue and Hack
entry.content:
🗡️ Rogue and Hack

🗡️ Rogue 🗡️ Hack

14 October 2026. Two dungeons, shipped the same day, on purpose. One of them ends. The other keeps the stairs going.

🗡️ Rogue

A small homage to the 1980 game. One room, a wall around it, you as 🧑.

The monsters are a kobold 👺, an orc 👹, a zombie 🧟, and a dragon 🐉. Deeper floors hold more of them, and the harder ones start to show up. Walk into a monster and you hit it. Stand next to one and it hits you back. Gold 💰 adds to the purse when you step on it. A potion 🧪 goes into your pack. Press Q to drink one and heal.

Every floor through the fifth has stairs 🔽. Step on them. Floor six has no stairs. It has the amulet 💎. Pick it up and the run is over. You won.

Arrows or WASD to move. R starts a new run from floor one, including after you die. Hit points start at 12. There is no save. A dead run is a dead run.

🗡️ Hack

Closer to the original shape. Rooms carved out of rock, corridors between them, stairs up ⬆️ and stairs down ⬇️.

Monsters are letters of a bestiary, drawn as pictures: ant, bat, centipede, dragon, floating eye, fungus, gnome, hobbit, imp, jackal, kobold, leprechaun. Deeper floors add more of them, and the ones that spawn hit harder and last longer. They walk toward you. If they reach you, they swing.

The floor also holds daggers, short swords, leather and chain, potions of healing, scrolls, and gold. Step on a thing and it goes into your pack. I prints the pack. Weapons add to what you hit for. Your strength starts at 16, your hit points at 20.

Move with the arrows, with WASD, or with the vi keys, diagonals included: y u b n, and q e z c. ? prints the reminder. R, or Enter on the death screen, starts again.

The win screen is written for the Amulet of Yendor. The dungeon you can walk today does not place one. The stairs keep going, and the question the game actually asks is whether you are still alive when you decide to stop.
entry.summary: Two dungeons. Rogue ends at an amulet on floor six. Hack keeps going down.

entry.title: 🚀 Galaxy Hunt, 🌲 Adventureland, 🏴‍☠️ Pirate Adventure
entry.content:
🚀 Galaxy Hunt, 🌲 Adventureland, 🏴‍☠️ Pirate Adventure

🚀 Galaxy Hunt 🌲 Adventureland 🏴‍☠️ Pirate Adventure

13 October 2026. Three games that want you to type.

🚀 Galaxy Hunt

A Super Star Trek, played from a green prompt. The galaxy is 8 by 8 quadrants. Some of them hold raider ships, some hold an alliance outpost, all of them hold stars.

The mission is on the opening screen: destroy every raider before the stardate runs out. Energy, missiles, and shields are finite. Dock by flying onto an outpost when the ship is falling apart. That resupplies and repairs you.

Commands, short on purpose:

  • NAV course warp — course is 1 to 9 around a compass rose, warp is 0.1 to 8
  • SRS and LRS — short-range map, long-range map
  • BEA energy — beams
  • MIS course — a missile
  • SHE energy — shields
  • DAM, COM, STA — damage, the library computer, status
  • HELP — the rose, the emoji key, and this list again
  • QUIT — abandon the mission

The map key is the hunter 🚀, a raider 👾, a star ⭐, an outpost 🏢, and a dot for empty space. Stars block you and they block missiles. Run out of energy, or out of time, and the mission fails.

🌲 Adventureland

The classic chain, White Witch edition. You start in a dark forest. A sleeping dragon occupies the meadow and does not like mud. There is a lake, a bog, a swamp, a cypress you can climb, and a hollow stump.

The stump is where the treasures go. There are thirteen of them. SCORE counts them out of 13.

Move with N S E W U D, or GO and a direction. LOOK, INVENTORY, GET, DROP. The puzzles that are not directions are on the help list, and they are exact: SAY BUNYON, SAY AWAY, RUB LAMP, LIGHT LAMP, UNLOCK DOOR, YELL, JUMP, FILL, CATCH, DAM, POUR. If a line comes back as “I don’t understand,” HELP is that list again.

🏴‍☠️ Pirate Adventure

You wake up in a London flat. A bookcase, a window, a book about pirates. East is the street, then the dock, a ship, a parrot, and a hold. South of the dock is the island: jungle, a clearing, a cave, a beach, a boat.

Three of the objects are the point. The chest of pirate gold, the bag of jewels, and the pile of coins are treasures. The book, the parrot, the anchor, the machete, the map, the bottle, and the key are how you get to them. The skeleton does not come with you.

Same shape as Adventureland. Directions, GET, DROP, and a few extra verbs: READ, OPEN, SAY, CLIMB, BOARD, FILL. SCORE tells you how many treasures you have secured. HELP if you would rather not guess.

Pieces of eight.
entry.summary: A starship, then two treasure hunts. Type HELP when a sentence bounces.

entry.title: 🏓 Pong and 🐍 Snake
entry.content:
🏓 Pong and 🐍 Snake

🏓 Pong 🐍 Snake

12 October 2026. The corner opened with the two games that fit in one sentence.

🏓 Pong

You on the left, the machine on the right, a ball between you. First to 5 wins.

Press S to start. W and S, or the up and down arrows, move your paddle. The machine follows the ball, a little late and a little short, which is the whole game. Each clean hit speeds the ball up. Miss, and the other side scores. R starts the match over.

The screen is a text field, forty columns by twenty rows, green on black, with a small beep when the ball meets something.

🐍 Snake

Same kind of screen. You are a line that grows.

Press S to start. Arrows or WASD turn. You cannot reverse into yourself. The apple is worth 10. Every 50 points the tick gets shorter, down to a floor where it will not get any faster.

The field is not empty. Cactus, rock, bomb, skull, fire, and lightning sit on it from the start, and running into one of them is the same as running into a wall or your own tail. R after the crash.

That was day one. Two games, both finished enough to lose.
entry.summary: Opening day. Pong, first to 5, and Snake on a field full of hazards.
